quizzes.title: Origin of International Labour Day: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: International Labour Day is observed each year in May to honour the contribution of workers across the world. Its origin is traced to the labour movement of the late nineteenth century in the United States, a period when workers were pressing for shorter working hours. In 1886, a large demonstration took place in America, and the gathering was an important moment for the movement. The events that followed in one city are known by their own name and are regarded as the point at which the day began. Several years later, socialist political organisations in another continent came together to choose a common date for the celebration. The observance then reached India in the early twentieth century, when the first May Day was celebrated in an Indian city by a political group. Today the day is recognised as a tribute to labour, and the booklet links its present theme to safety and health at work in a changing climate. The booklet presents the day as a reminder of the demands that workers made over a century ago, and of the way those demands shaped later observances.

questions.q: According to the 1886 demonstration in America, workers demanded how many hours of work on a daily basis?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the 1886 demonstration demanded 8 hours of work on a daily basis.

questions.q: In 1923, the first May Day in India was celebrated in which city?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the first May Day in India was celebrated in Chennai (then Madras) in 1923.

questions.q: In 1889, Socialist Parties in which region decided to celebrate May 1 as International Labour Day?
questions.explanation: The booklet records that Socialist Parties in Europe made this decision in 1889.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Many people were hurt during the 1886 demonstration in Chicago.
Reason (R): The demonstration went out of hand in Chicago.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says the demonstration went out of hand and many people got hurt, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Haymarket Affair   ->   A. Socialist Parties' decision to celebrate May 1 (1889)
II. Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan   ->   B. Also known as Workers Day
III. 1889 decision on the date   ->   C. Incident that marked the start of the day
IV. Workers Day   ->   D. First May Day in India (1923)
questions.explanation: The Haymarket Affair marked the start of the day, the Labour Kisan Party organised the 1923 May Day, the 1889 decision is the socialist one, and Workers Day is another name.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the origin of International Labour Day:
I. The first May Day in India was celebrated in 1923.
II. The Haymarket Affair took place in 1889.
III. Socialist Parties in Europe decided on May 1 in 1889.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the first Indian May Day to 1923 and the Socialist Parties' decision to 1889, while the Haymarket Affair is linked to the 1886 demonstration.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about International Labour Day:
I. It is observed each year on May 1.
II. The 1886 demonstration demanded a ten-hour working day.
III. It is also known as Workers Day.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, but the 1886 demand was for 8 hours, so statement II is wrong and only two are correct.

quizzes.title: Origin of International Labour Day: TITA practice
quizzes.passage: International Labour Day is observed every year in May to honour the contribution of workers across the world. The day is also known as Workers Day or May Day. Its beginnings are linked to the labour movement of the late nineteenth century in the United States, where workers were pressing for shorter working hours. In 1886, a large demonstration took place in America, but it soon went out of hand, and in one city many people were hurt. The incident that followed is remembered as a turning point and is regarded as the point at which the day began. Several years later, socialist political organisations in another continent agreed to adopt a single date for labour observance. The observance reached India in the early twentieth century, when the first celebration in the country was held in an Indian city by a political group of workers and peasants. The booklet presents the day as a tribute to labour. The theme for 2026 is Ensuring Safety and Health at Work in A Changing Climate, and the observance is therefore linked to that present-day concern.

questions.q: In 1889, Socialist Parties in which continent decided to celebrate May 1 as International Labour Day?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Socialist Parties in Europe made the decision in 1889.

questions.q: In which year was the first May Day celebrated in India?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the first May Day celebration in India to 1923.

questions.q: The first May Day in India was celebrated in which city, then known as Madras?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Chennai (then Madras) as the city of the 1923 celebration.

questions.q: The 1886 demonstration in America demanded how many hours of work on a daily basis? (number of hours)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 1886 demonstration demanded 8 hours of work on a daily basis.

questions.q: What is the name of the Chicago incident that marked the start of International Labour Day?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the incident in Chicago that followed the 1886 demonstration is known as the Haymarket Affair.

questions.q: On which day of May is International Labour Day observed? (day number)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that International Labour Day takes place annually on May 1.

questions.q: Which political party organised the first May Day celebration in India in 1923? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 1923 celebration was held by the Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan.

quizzes.title: ILO objectives, standards and reports: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: The International Labour Organisation is a specialised agency of the United Nations, dedicated to improving labour conditions and living standards throughout the world. It promotes social justice and internationally recognised human and labour rights, and it is an integral part of the United Nations Human Rights Framework. The organisation sets out stated objectives that cover fundamental labour rights, greater opportunities for women and men, social protection, and social dialogue. Its international labour standards are legal instruments drawn up by its constituents, namely governments, employers and workers, and they set out basic principles and rights at work. Such standards come in more than one form, and each form carries a different status. The ILO also issues a declaration on fundamental principles and rights at work, which names several focus areas for member states. Finally, the organisation publishes key reports that examine employment, wages and social protection across the world, and these reports help track conditions in the world of work.

questions.q: Which of the following is a focus area of the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists elimination of employment discrimination among the declaration's focus areas.

questions.q: Which of the ILO's international labour standards are described as non-binding guidelines?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Recommendations as non-binding guidelines, while Conventions and Protocols are legally binding.

questions.q: What does the ILO's tripartite structure give to governments, employers and workers?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the tripartite structure gives governments, employers and workers an equal voice.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Recommendations of the ILO cannot be enforced as legal obligations.
Reason (R): Recommendations are non-binding guidelines.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Because recommendations are non-binding guidelines, they do not operate as legal obligations, so R explains A.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Forced Labour Convention   ->   A. No. 111
II. Equal Remuneration Convention   ->   B. No. 29
III. Discrimination Convention   ->   C. No. 182
IV. Worst Forms of Child Labour Convention   ->   D. No. 100
questions.explanation: Forced Labour is No. 29, Equal Remuneration is No. 100, Discrimination is No. 111 and Worst Forms of Child Labour is No. 182.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ILO:
I. The ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work was amended in 2022.
II. Recommendations are legally binding on member states.
III. Freedom of association is among the focus areas of the ILO Declaration.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The booklet confirms the 2022 amendment and freedom of association as a focus area, while recommendations are non-binding.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ILO standards and objectives:
I. Conventions and Protocols are legally binding international treaties.
II. Recommendations are legally binding treaties.
III. The ILO pursues four stated objectives.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because recommendations are non-binding, so only two are correct.

quizzes.title: ILO objectives, standards and reports: TITA practice
quizzes.passage: The International Labour Organisation was set up to improve labour conditions and living standards across the world. It is a specialised agency of the United Nations devoted to promoting social justice and internationally recognised human and labour rights, and it is an integral part of the United Nations Human Rights Framework. The organisation pursues several objectives, including promoting fundamental labour rights, creating greater opportunities for women and men, enhancing social protection and strengthening social dialogue. Its international labour standards are drawn up by its constituents, namely governments, employers and workers, and include Conventions, Protocols and Recommendations. One important document is a declaration on fundamental principles and rights at work, which names focus areas such as freedom of association, the elimination of forced labour and the abolition of child labour. The ILO also publishes several key reports, including one focused on wages and another on the world of work.

questions.q: Which ILO convention number deals with Forced Labour? (give the number)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Forced Labour Convention as No. 29.

questions.q: In which year was the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work amended?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the declaration, adopted in 1998, was amended in 2022.

questions.q: Which word describes the ILO structure that gives governments, employers and workers an equal voice? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the ILO's unique feature as its tripartite structure.

questions.q: Which ILO convention number deals with Equal Remuneration? (give the number)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Equal Remuneration as Convention No. 100.

questions.q: Which treaty is listed as the establishment basis of the ILO? (name of the treaty)
questions.explanation: The booklet's overview lists the Treaty of Versailles under the ILO's establishment.

questions.q: Which key ILO report focuses on wages? (name of the report)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Global Wage Report among the ILO's key reports.

questions.q: Which ILO convention number deals with the Worst Forms of Child Labour? (give the number)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Worst Forms of Child Labour as Convention No. 182.
